examples.9.1 Glossary: Moonshift defines shift as one timed puzzle session that ends with a room restored or a retry, and room as one air network with a fixed fault set. Vertical slice means the 15-minute final-quality build due in week 12, not the whole demo. Mateo Chen edits the glossary, and every new term gets a tab link before it enters the GDD.
examples.9.2 Decision log: ADR-001, dated 11 February 2026, locks Moonshift to single-player because co-op would add 14 weeks and server cost; async sharing and local co-op were rejected. ADR-002 fixes the isometric camera after free orbit failed readability tests at tablet size. ADR-003 cuts room decoration from launch, and ADR-011 supersedes it by moving that work to the post-launch expansion if sales reach 20,000.
examples.9.3 Open questions tracker: Q-001 asks whether Switch ships at launch or after PC and tablet; the producer must answer by week 8. Q-002 is open on accepting PEGI 7 for the alarm imagery, due week 12. Q-003 is answered yes: the demo save carries into the full game, and Q-004 defers the paid expansion question to the launch review.
examples.9.4 Reference library: The certification folder holds the current platform TRC at /references/cert/platform-trc-2026.pdf, owned by the producer and checked at beta. The accessibility baseline is the 2026 Game Accessibility Guidelines, the art team cites the Outlanders teardown for readability, and legal keeps the COPPA and GDPR guidance. The playtest consent template at /references/research/consent-v3.docx is required before recording any minor.
examples.9.5 Asset and dependency tracker: The final logo is on track for week 10, but the trademark search is still pending. The main theme is at risk because the composer contract is unsigned, the text freeze is on track for week 24, and the console dev kit is late pending a platform application. The age-rating submission has not started because it needs the final build.
examples.9.6 Meeting and playtest notes template: On 14 May 2026, build 0.8.3-rc2 was tested with five players aged 9–12 and two observers. Hypothesis: players would understand the airlock loop without a prompt; four of five skipped the tutorial card and one read the resource bar as health. Decisions: move the prompt inline and label the storm warning safe; actions go to the UX writer by 18 May and a re-test by 28 May.
examples.9.7 Version history and sign-off: Version 0.1 on 3 February 2026 was the first draft of scope, milestones, and budget, approved by Ana Rivera. Version 0.2 added the risk register and certification checklist on 17 March, and version 1.0 locked launch scope and the T-90 checklist on 2 April. Ana Rivera, Mateo Chen, Jon Okafor, Sana Patel, and Lina Novak signed the 1.0 tab on 2–3 April.
